free_text_notes:
Summary: This 'sliver' audit focused on low-footprint pools where idle fragmentation is driving extra headroom cost. Key signals: (1) apac ephemeral pools show high idle fragmentation (>25%) from many small jobs; (2) eu priority-medium is functionally saturated at p95 and will need short-term burst capacity or priority rebalancing; (3) global serve-critical pool is near its safety margin and has had multiple preemptions in the last 48h. Immediate actions: 1) schedule a packing experiment for reserved-large in us-west-1 to co-locate long-running servers into fewer slices (owner: Miguel Torres, due: 2026-12-28); 2) throttle small-job prewarm in apac ephemeral pools and enable prefix cache for repeated seeds (owner: Lena Wu, due: 2026-12-26); 3) allocate +20 GPUs from spot-scratch to priority-medium for 72h controlled burst (owner: Arjun Patel, jira INFRA-4821). Follow-ups: run 24h microburst sim with current enqueue distribution and report p95 change; reconcile allocation rules for preemption-sensitive workloads.

Notes on methodology: table exported from dashboard snapshot at 2026-12-21T14:02Z (UTC). avg_used_gpus is mean over 24h sampled at 1m. p50/p95 are percentage of total_gpus used. headroom_gpus = total_gpus - p95_used_gpus. idle_fragmentation_pct computed as portion of GPU slices with <10% utilization averaged across pool. avg_enqueue_ms is median enqueue latency for requests that started in window. scheduled_jobs_count is number of unique job ids scheduled in window. Preemptions are counted at job-level.

Observations for planning cycle: - If apac idle fragmentation remains >20% we recommend a policy change to prefer 1–2 GPU jobs on shared dev pools only during 00:00–08:00 UTC; - For eu priority pools, add a temporary dedicated slice or promote reserved capacity until INFRA-4821 is resolved; - Add metric 'slice_fill_rate' to daily export to better quantify packing opportunity.
